newsitem.title: CHINA: Dirty syringes infect 26 people in Chinese city.
newsitem.headline: Dirty syringes infect 26 people in Chinese city.

text.p: At least 26 people in central China have been infected after receiving injections using re-used disposable syringes picked out of hospital dustbins and resold to clinics, officials said on Wednesday.
"About 10 people are still in hospital now," an official of the Changde Public Health Bureau in central Hunan province told Reuters by telephone.
In early April, about 26 people in Changde city were seriously infected after injections with syringes provided by a medical company under the city's Epidemic Prevention Station, the official said.

The medical company had bought 73,800 syringes from private salesman Qiu Lin, who was alleged to have collected them from dustbins outside hospitals in central Jiangxi province and had sold 45,200 to hospitals and clinics in Changde, he said.
The company manager was suspected of taking a commission, the Legal Daily newspaper said.
Qiu Lin, who posed as a salesman for a Shanghai medical company, went missing after being fined 5,000 yuan ($602) by the local Administration for Industry and Commerce, he said.
